title: Yekatit 12 massacre
summary: After grenades wounded the Italian viceroy Rodolfo Graziani at Addis Ababa on 19 February 1937, Italian soldiers, Blackshirts and civilians killed Ethiopians in the capital for about three days and burned homes. Estimates of the dead range from about 1,400 to 30,000; arrests and executions followed.

uncertainty.note: Sources give the start as 19 February 1937 and a duration of three days; reprisals and executions continued afterwards.

as_recorded.value: occurred on February 19, 1937; the three days that followed

where.modern_name: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia (Genete Leul Palace, Sidist Kilo, Arada)
where.historical_name: Addis Ababa, capital of Italian East Africa (Ethiopia under Italian occupation)

importance.justification: The deadliest single episode of reprisal during the Italian occupation of Ethiopia; commemorated annually in Ethiopia.

audience_note: Describes mass killing of civilians, including burning of homes and bodies; the death toll is disputed.

sources.title: The worst massacre in Ethiopia's history
The Addis Ababa Massacre: Italy's National Shame (publisher page)
sources.author: Ian L. Campbell

sources.title: Wikidata item Q3624 (Addis Ababa), coordinate location (P625)

reviewer_note: Death toll reported as a range: 1,400-6,000 (newspapers and others), about 3,000 (Mockler, Del Boca), about 19,000-19,200 (Campbell 2017, roughly 19-20% of the city), 30,000 (Ethiopian authorities), as listed on the opened pages; not adjudicated. End date 21 Feb is inferred from "three days". The second source is a publisher page, not the book itself. The memorial in Sidist Kilo and Debre Libanos reprisal are not covered.
